low: Walk for 10 minutes after one meal each day.
Stand up and move for 2 minutes every hour you sit.
Do 5 sit-to-stands from a chair, twice a day.
mid: Reach 150 minutes this week: five 30-minute brisk walks.
Add two 15-minute strength sessions: squats, counter push-ups, band rows.
Take the stairs or a walking call every workday.
high: Add one harder session: intervals or hills for 20 minutes.
Progress your strength work: a little more weight or one more set.
Schedule one full rest or easy day and protect it.

low: Add one vegetable or fruit to the meal you eat most often.
Swap one sugary drink a day for water or unsweetened tea.
Put a palm-sized portion of protein on your plate at breakfast or lunch.
mid: Fill half your plate with vegetables at dinner, five nights this week.
Plan and shop for three home-cooked dinners.
Keep fruit, nuts or plain yoghurt where snacks usually sit.
high: Reach 30 g of fibre a day; count it for three days to check.
Try two vegetables or pulses you rarely cook.
Cook a double batch once and freeze portions for busy nights.

low: Set one wake-up time and keep it all seven days.
Charge your phone outside the bedroom.
mid: Add a 20-minute wind-down: dim lights, no work, same order every night.
Get 10 minutes of outdoor light within an hour of waking.
Make the bedroom cool, dark and quiet; fix the weakest of the three.
high: Keep weekend sleep within an hour of weekday times.
Finish hard exercise and heavy meals at least 3 hours before bed.
Note how rested you feel for a week, then shift bedtime by 15 minutes if needed.

low: Do one minute of slow breathing when you sit down to work.
Write down the one thing that must get done today, then do it first.
Take a 10-minute walk outside without your phone.
mid: Practise box breathing for 3 minutes, twice a day.
Keep two phone-free blocks: 30 minutes after waking and 30 before bed.
Name what is stressing you and one step you control; write both down.
high: Try a 10-minute daily mindfulness, prayer or journalling practice.
Plan one session this week for a hobby that absorbs you.
Do a weekly review: what gave you energy, what drained it, one change.

low: Send one message today to someone you have not spoken to in a while.
Say yes to one invitation this week, or make one.
Share one meal with another person, phones away.
mid: Put a standing weekly call or walk with a friend in your calendar.
Join one group built around something you enjoy: a class, club, team or faith community.
Do one small favour for a neighbour or colleague.
high: Host something simple: coffee, a walk or a shared meal.
Give an hour to a cause you care about.
Check in on someone who may be lonely.
tool: Steps calculator for a walk with a friend

low: Book the checkup you have been putting off.
Measure your blood pressure at a pharmacy or at home and write it down.
Pick two alcohol-free days this week.
mid: Measure your waist and work out your waist-to-height ratio.
Check which screenings and vaccines are due for your age.
If you smoke, set a quit date and tell one person.
high: Record blood pressure morning and evening for a week to learn your true average.
Ask your doctor for your cholesterol and blood sugar results, and keep them.
Help a family member book their overdue checkup.
